subject: Post-demo: DPA request and SCC module preference + controller/processor alignment
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@aureonhealth.com>, Priya Das <priya.das@aureonhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + DPA / SCC question after today's demo

Hi Amir / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the discussion and the clear signal that data residency, DPA language, and SCC routing are the gating items for procurement. Per our call, I wanted to capture next steps and a couple of clarifying asks so we can move legal review in parallel with technical onboarding.

Recap / fast answers:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (security, availability) in Q4 2025. I attached a 1-page summary below for quick review.
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA-covered workflows via our Private deployment option (VPC + BAAs).
- GDPR / DPA: we typically execute a DPA with customers; by default Redwood is the processor and customer is the controller, but there are some edge cases (analytics/derived data) we should call out.

Open asks for you (so legal can start review):
1) DPA: will Aureon request Redwood to sign your standard DPA or would you prefer Redwood's template? Either is fine — we can map redlines.
2) SCC module preference: your legal team mentioned wanting the SCC 'controller-to-processor' flow vs 'processor-to-processor' — can you confirm which module your counsel prefers? If unsure, let us know the language they expect and we can recommend the module.
3) Controller designations: please confirm whether Aureon will be sole controller for patient-identifiable inputs (most common) or if you expect any shared-controller constructs for joint features.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the DPA template preference and SCC module + any flagged clauses (due EOD Wed).
- I'll loop Legal (cc'd Rishi and Laura) and send our DPA draft + SOC2 summary and a vendor questionnaire starter.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call (we can bring our counsel).

Attachments: SOC2-QuickSummary-2025.pdf (one-pager)

Thanks — short items will unblock procurement.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

---

From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@aureonhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Das <priya.das@aureonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + DPA / SCC question after today's demo

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick answers from our side:
1) DPA template: our procurement team prefers vendors to review our standard DPA first — I'll attach it to the procurement request. If Redwood prefers to circulate your template in parallel, that's fine.
2) SCC module: our counsel tends to push for the controller-to-processor flow (Module 2 in our playbook) for SaaS ingest of personal data.
3) Controller designation: Aureon will be the sole controller for patient-identifiable inputs; we expect Redwood to be the processor.

We do need to kick off a lightweight vendor security questionnaire (30–40 questions) for standard intake. Can you send the questionnaire or a summary of your controls so our team can triage?

We'll aim to turn the DPA review in 5–7 business days once we have your draft. If you could also include the SOC2 one-pager and any SOC2 letter/evidence pointers, that would speed us up.

Best,
Amir
Head of Product, Aureon Health
amir.khan@aureonhealth.com | (212) 555-0910

On Jun 1, 2026, Sofia Ivanova wrote:

> Thanks again for your time today...

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA routing / SCC module question for Aureon Health

Sofia / Rishi —

Quick legal guidance to help craft the draft and the ask to Aureon:

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood's standard position is Processor. Confirmed — we should not accept controller designation unless scope specifically requires Redwood to determine purposes/means of processing (unlikely for standard inference). I will mark "Processor" in the DPA and include the standard carveouts for aggregated analytics (we can provide an opt-out if Aureon objects).

2) SCC module recommendation: Because Aureon will be exporting personal data from EU/UK regions in some workflows, recommend we propose the Controller-to-Processor SCC module (Module 2) as Amir indicated. That's the least friction path.

3) DPA redlines to expect: data subject rights handling, subprocessors list + 30-day notice for new subprocessors, data retention limits tied to retention schedule, and standard liability caps. I'll pre-populate our DPA draft with those items.

4) SOC2 evidence: attach the one-pager and include a link to a redacted SOC2 letter (we can't circulate full report without NDA). Offer to set up a secure evidence room if they need more.

I'll prepare a DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Draft.pdf) and a short vendor questionnaire starter (we can reuse our 40-question intake). Sofia, once you have Amir's DPA or confirmation they want us to review theirs, I can run parallel edits.

Cc: Rishi — can you confirm if the customer will need HIPAA BAAs at this stage? From discussion it sounded like they are evaluating, but not required for initial POC.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Hi Amir / Priya —

Thanks — that's helpful. Per Laura's note below, I've attached our DPA draft and the SOC2 one-pager for your procurement/legal team to triage. Also attaching a 10-question vendor-security starter (we call it "VQ-lite") that maps to our full questionnaire and should be quick to answer to prioritize high-risk items.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_Draft.pdf (DPA draft) | SOC2-QuickSummary-2025.pdf | VQ-lite-10q.xlsx (attachment stub)

Suggested next steps:
- Procurement: share your DPA if you want Redwood to review it; otherwise review our draft and send redlines.
- Legal: confirm SCC Module 2 (controller-to-processor) is acceptable; if so we will mark Module 2 in the DPA.
- Tech: if you want a brief security/arch review, we can set a 30-min call with our infra lead (we can do Tue/Thu afternoons next week).

Would you like me to open a HubSpot legal ticket or shall I wait for your DPA to be attached to the procurement request?

I'll follow up on Friday if I don't hear back.

Best,
Sofia
